transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-29 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Turner (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortega (CTO, Mosaic), Priya Menon (Head of Security), Liam Chow (Eng Manager), Sara Lee (PM)

Summary:
Quick POC kickoff to agree success criteria for credential/PII redaction across chat and form-insert flows, decide what telemetry we capture during the pilot, and scope benchmark windows for throughput/latency. Customer prefers Private deployment if KMS + audit chain works, but open to Dedicated for speed.

Topics covered: PII redaction approach, prompt storage TTLs, what counts as "sensitive" (credentials, ssn-like, tokens), telemetry sampling, bench sizes and run cadence, success criteria for go/no-go.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Alex: okay everyone thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood - we'll keep this to about 45 minutes, my SE Priya is here to dig into the technicals. Could you quick intro?
[00:00:10] Daniel: yeah, I'm Daniel CTO at Mosaic, we run a hybrid checkout and a returns assistant that surfaces customer account info — biggest concern is accidental credential leakage in prompts and retention.
[00:00:20] Priya Menon: hi all, Priya here, head of security, SOC2 in process, need to know how long prompts are stored and whether redaction happens before write to logs.
[00:00:30] Priya Shah: thanks Priya. short answer: Redwood can redact at ingestion with configurable patterns, and you can choose to not persist raw prompt text in the hosted flow, but we'll walk through tradeoffs.
[00:00:40] Liam: quick clarifying q: when you say redact at ingestion, is that before HLN caching or after? we use KV cache heavily for session continuity.
[00:00:50] Priya Shah: great question. by default we can run a lightweight PII detection step pre-cache; if you want deterministic redaction we recommend the private deployment with local KMS so keys never leave your vault. that avoids storing raw text in any shared cache.
[00:01:05] Daniel: so Private deploy = all logs stay in our VPC? or do audit logs still stream out?
[00:01:12] Alex: with Redwood Private the control plane is customer-managed, logs can be kept in your account, and we support pushing audit events to your SIEM. for Hosted/Dedicated we have retention controls but logs are in Redwood-managed infra unless you opt for log-forwarding.
[00:01:26] Priya Menon: how about KMS — do you support customer KMS and HSM?
[00:01:30] Priya Shah: yes, we support customer KMS via standard envelopes and HSM-backed keys for critical flows. note: there is a small perf delta for HSM unwraps but it's usually sub-10ms per request.
[00:01:45] Sara: on retention TTL, can we have different retention by route? e.g., sensitive form submissions expire after 24h, diagnostics 90 days?
[00:01:52] Priya Shah: yep, policy is per-route or per-model; you can configure a retention TTL and also a mode where we store only vector embeddings (no raw prompt) for analytics.
[00:02:05] Daniel: ok let's talk about benching — we have peak checkout traffic ~120 reqs/sec, avg prompt length 180 tokens, response avg 220 tokens. we want p95 < 350ms for the live assistant.
[00:02:18] Alex: good concrete numbers — for the POC we should replicate a 5 minute peak window, plus a 30 minute normal traffic baseline. SE: what's the expected hardware?
[00:02:27] Priya Shah: depends on model; if you want the fastest latency we'll suggest a quantized 8-bit variant on Dedicated GPUs; for privacy-first we'd run Private on your infra with the same runtime. for throughput: to simulate 120 rps with 400 token total payloads we recommend a 20-minute sustained run and a 5 minute spike test.
[00:02:45] Liam: is there anything special about token billing during tests? like do cached prefixes change effective tokens?
[00:02:50] Priya Shah: yes cached prefixes reduce billable compute and tokens; for bench parity we'll disable prefix caching for the spike test and enable realistic caching for the baseline run. just something to document in the spreadsheet.
[00:03:05] Daniel: we also need to ensure no credentials are recorded in any logs if possible, right?
[00:03:10] Priya Shah: you can configure redaction that removes or hashes credential-like strings before writes. there are three modes: detect-and-flag (for manual triage), mask-in-place (****), and drop-field (remove the entire field). we recommend mask-in-place for chat UI and drop-field for backend tokens.
[00:03:28] Priya Menon: can the detection be tuned? our token patterns include order numbers that look like SSNs sometimes so we need low false positives.
[00:03:35] Priya Shah: absolutely — regex + ML heuristics. we'll supply default patterns and you can provide exceptions. that's part of what I'll send in the redaction-patterns doc.
[00:03:47] Alex: any legal / procurement ask up front?
[00:03:50] Daniel: we need standard DPA and SLA for pilot; procurement wants to see sample contract language.
[00:03:55] Alex: we'll route that via our CSM and legal; I'll attach the DPA and our pilot T&Cs.
[00:04:05] Sara: regarding telemetry, what exactly will you capture during the POC? token counts, latency, top error types?
[00:04:10] Priya Shah: we capture token-level cost, per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), error codes, and model fallback events. for PII-sensitive flows we can redact the prompt in telemetry and only capture structured metadata.
[00:04:22] Liam: do you sample payloads for QA? we need to be able to QA some responses but not expose PII.
[00:04:26] Priya Shah: sampling is configurable — you can whitelist intents and only sample non-sensitive responses, or we can run automated redaction on samples before sending them to QA.
[00:04:38] Daniel: timeline wise — if we get the spreadsheet and sample traces by next week can we run a benchmark the following week?
[00:04:43] Alex: yes that aligns. Priya SE, do you have capacity week of Nov 8 for a 2-hour window plus pre-setup?
[00:04:50] Priya Shah: yes tentative. we'll need SSH access to your test harness for Private baseline or a load generator endpoint for Dedicated.
[00:04:58] Daniel: about success criteria — here's what we propose: zero recorded credentials in logs, p95 < 350ms on live intent, and equiv output quality compared to current model (we'll provide a QA prompt set).
[00:05:10] Priya Menon: add: audit log chain demonstrating KMS unwrap events for any decrypted payloads.
[00:05:15] Alex: noted. we'll include KMS unwrap events in the audit trail for the pilot.
[00:05:20] Sara: any bandwidth concerns for the Private deploy? we might need a sizing doc.
[00:05:24] Priya Shah: we'll share a sizing worksheet — CPU/GPU needs scale with model and token throughput; for 120 rps and 400 token payloads typical Dedicated SLOs map to X GPUs, we'll put numbers in the sheet.
[00:05:36] Liam: can Redwood run the bench remotely while we're on Dedicated? or do we need to coordinate on-prem?
[00:05:41] Alex: we can run it remotely against Dedicated endpoint or coordinate a Private on-prem run. remote is easier for speed.
[00:05:49] Daniel: one more security question: are prompts encrypted at rest in your hosted offering?
[00:05:54] Priya Shah: hosted: encrypted at rest with our keys by default, customer-managed KMS option for Private/Dedicated. we also support field-level encryption.
[00:06:04] Priya Menon: ok please document where raw prompts land in each deployment mode, we need that for our audit.
[00:06:09] Alex: will do. I'll include a matrix in the follow-up.
[00:06:12] Daniel: great. any blockers on Redwood side?
[00:06:15] Priya Shah: just need the workload CSV and the top-10 intents plus your retention policy table. I'll also draft a redaction test plan — send back with examples.
[00:06:24] Sara: regarding QA — we want a canary rollout approach for the pilot, 10% traffic holdback, validate redaction and latency before full switch.
[00:06:31] Alex: Redwood supports canary A/B at the routing layer; we'll set that up and include automatic rollback on error thresholds.
[00:06:38] Liam: any known gotchas about telemetry skew when you enable redaction? like token counts changing?
[00:06:43] Priya Shah: redaction can change tokenization in edge cases; we recommend measuring both pre-redaction and post-redaction token counts in the bench so we can correlate cost delta.
[00:06:55] Daniel: ok wrap up, let's confirm deliverables and dates.
[00:07:00] Alex: recap - Redwood will: 1) send redaction-patterns doc + KMS notes by 2026-11-02, 2) provide bench template and sizing worksheet today, 3) schedule SE-led benchmark week of 2026-11-08 pending customer data. Customer will: provide workload CSV and traces by 2026-11-03, and the QA prompt set by 2026-11-04.
[00:07:20] Priya Menon: sounds good. also follow-up with SOC2 artifact list for our compliance team.
[00:07:25] Alex: will loop in CSM/legal. thanks everyone.
[00:07:29] Daniel: thx all bye.
